The classification also includes specific types of permanent-magnetic synchronous mechanisms, which offer distinct advantages in certain operational environments, particularly where precision and reliability are critical.

name: Slip coupling
definition: this classification encompasses a type of mechanical connector designed to transmit torque between two rotating shafts while allowing for relative movement. Unlike other types of connectors, this specific type accommodates misalignment and provides a level of slip, which can help protect machinery from damage due to overload conditions. The design may incorporate various mechanisms, such as hydraulic or magnetic principles, to achieve the desired performance. This category is distinct from rigid, torsionally stiff, elastic, engaging, disengaging, and overload coupling types, offering unique functionality suited for specific applications in machinery and equipment. The focus is on facilitating smooth operation while mitigating the risks associated with misalignment and unexpected loads.

name: Overload coupling (Torque limiter)
definition: this classification pertains to devices designed to protect machinery by limiting torque transmission between rotational components. Such devices are crucial in preventing damage due to excessive force, ensuring operational safety and efficiency. They operate by engaging or disengaging based on the torque levels detected, providing a mechanism for energy transfer that can absorb shocks or overloads. The specific types include those that function through translation, friction engagement, or interlocking mechanisms, each serving to enhance the reliability of mechanical assemblies in various applications. These devices are essential in diverse industries where rotational power transmission is involved, offering vital protection and control features.

name: Coupling with measuring sensor
definition: this category encompasses devices designed to connect two or more components while incorporating measuring sensors to monitor parameters such as tension, pressure, or displacement. These devices facilitate the transmission of torque or motion while providing real-time data on operational conditions. The integration of sensing technology allows for enhanced performance monitoring, ensuring optimal functionality and safety in various applications. This classification is distinct from other types of couplings that focus solely on mechanical connection without the incorporation of measurement capabilities. The devices in this category are utilized in a range of industries where precise measurements are critical to system performance and reliability.

name: Component for coupling
definition: Definition is still due

name: Coupling (non-electric, other)
definition: Group (3rd level) for objects that cannot be classified into other specified groups in the existing structure, but that are classified to their parent-class on the 2nd level. A xx-xx-90-00-class cannot have any other sub-groups besides the generic xx-xx-90-90-class (…(Other, unspecified)) to be generally valid within the parent class on the 2nd level

name: Mechanical brake
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed to slow down or stop the motion of machinery and vehicles through mechanical means. These devices utilize various mechanical components and principles to create friction or resistance, effectively controlling speed and movement. Unlike other braking systems that rely on electrical or fluid forces, this category focuses on systems that operate through physical mechanisms, such as levers, springs, and friction materials. Included within this classification are various specific types of mechanical brakes, each employing distinct operational methods and applications to serve different industrial and automotive purposes.

name: Electric brake
definition: a mechanism designed to reduce the speed or halt the movement of a machine or vehicle by employing electrical energy as the primary means of operation. This type of braking system utilizes various principles of electromagnetism to create resistance against motion. Unlike other braking systems that rely on mechanical or hydraulic forces, this approach is characterized by its ability to provide precise control and rapid response. The specific implementations within this category include systems that utilize magnetic powder, eddy currents, and hysteresis effects to achieve effective braking performance. These systems are particularly suited for applications requiring high reliability and efficiency in braking operations.

name: Fluid brake
definition: a category that encompasses devices designed to slow down or halt the movement of machinery or vehicles through the use of fluid dynamics. These systems utilize hydraulic or pneumatic principles to create resistance, thereby converting kinetic energy into thermal energy. They are characterized by their ability to provide smooth and controlled braking action, making them suitable for various applications where precision and reliability are paramount. This category is distinct from other braking mechanisms that rely on mechanical or electrical means, highlighting the unique operational principles of fluid-based systems.

name: Brake (other)
definition: Group (3rd level) for objects that cannot be classified into other specified groups in the existing structure, but that are classified to their parent-class on the 2nd level. A xx-xx-90-00-class cannot have any other sub-groups besides the generic xx-xx-90-90-class (…(Other, unspecified)) to be generally valid within the parent class on the 2nd level

name: Plain bearing
definition: this classification encompasses a variety of bearing types characterized by their ability to provide support and reduce friction between moving parts, utilizing surfaces that are smooth and typically cylindrical. The items within this category operate without rolling elements and can be employed in diverse applications, where they facilitate rotational or linear motion. They may utilize various principles, such as dry friction or fluid dynamics, to achieve performance efficiency. This classification specifically includes bearing types that utilize air or magnetic fields for support, as well as those designed for specialized movements, such as spherical or tilting pad configurations. These components are integral to machinery and equipment, contributing to their overall functionality and reliability while ensuring reduced wear and maintenance requirements.

name: Linear element
definition: this classification encompasses a range of components and assemblies specifically designed to facilitate linear motion and support. The focus is on elements that provide guidance and support for moving parts, ensuring smooth operation and stability during linear movement. This category includes specialized bearings and housings that enable motion along a predetermined path, as well as support structures that maintain alignment. The items categorized here are integral to linear systems, enhancing performance and reliability in various applications. This classification does not include other types of bearings or their components that serve different purposes or functionalities.

name: Radial ball bearing
definition: this classification encompasses a specific type of mechanical component designed to facilitate rotational or linear motion by reducing friction between moving parts. The items within this category are characterized by their spherical geometry, allowing for smooth operation and support of radial loads. They are distinct from other bearing types due to their unique construction and operational principles. This classification includes various forms that cater to different applications and load requirements, ensuring efficient performance in diverse mechanical systems. The components classified here are essential for maintaining the functionality of machinery, enhancing durability, and ensuring reliability in motion applications.

name: Radial roller bearing
definition: a type of mechanical component designed to facilitate the rotation or movement of adjacent parts while minimizing friction. This category encompasses various designs that utilize cylindrical or needle-shaped rolling elements to support radial loads. These components are characterized by their ability to handle both radial and axial forces, contributing to the efficient operation of machinery. They are essential in applications requiring high rigidity and load-carrying capacity. The range includes products with distinct configurations and features, tailored for specific operational needs. The classification covers several variations, each optimized for durability and performance in various environments, ensuring reliability in demanding applications.

name: Thrust ball bearing
definition: this classification encompasses a specific category of mechanical components designed to support axial loads while allowing for rotational motion. These items are characterized by their ability to transmit force along a shaft, facilitating smooth operation in various applications. The components in this category are distinct from other types of bearings that primarily handle radial loads or combined loading conditions. name: Thrust roller bearing
definition: this classification encompasses a specific type of bearing designed to accommodate axial loads, which are forces acting along the axis of the bearing. These components are engineered to provide support and reduce friction between moving parts, thus facilitating smooth rotational motion. Various designs are included, each tailored for different applications and load capacities, ensuring optimal performance in diverse environments. The offering includes distinct variations characterized by their roller types, such as cylindrical, needle, spherical, and tapered configurations. These variations allow for adaptability in a wide range of mechanical systems, enhancing efficiency and reliability. This classification is distinct from other bearing types that focus on radial loads or different operational functionalities.

The classification distinguishes these devices from other types of bearings by their specific design and operational capabilities, which cater to applications requiring rotational movement that differs from linear or purely radial bearings.

name: Sliding guide
definition: a sliding guide is a mechanical linear guide component where two surfaces slide directly against each other without rolling elements such as balls or rollers. the motion is based on sliding friction, making the design compact, resistant to dirt, and often maintenance-friendly. sliding guides are typically used in applications with low to moderate loads and moderate precision requirements, such as adjustment mechanisms, packaging machines, or basic linear units.

name: Cam roller guide
definition: cam roller guide systems are linear guide systems in which carriages with integrated rollers move along specially profiled rails. they provide a robust, smooth-running, and low-maintenance solution for linear motion in industrial applications.

name: Linear ball bearing guide
definition: linear ball bearing guide systems consist of shafts, ball bearings, and associated housings. they enable precise, low-friction linear motion using rolling elements.

name: Profiled rail guide
definition: profile rail guide systems are high-precision linear systems with carriages running on profiled rails. they offer high load capacity, rigidity, and accuracy.

name: Cage rail guide
definition: cage-guided linear guide systems are high-precision linear systems in which rolling elements such as balls, rollers, or needles are guided in a cage that moves between two profiled rails. the cage prevents the rolling elements from contacting each other, reducing friction, noise, and wear. thanks to their compact design and high rigidity, they are ideal for applications with limited space and high accuracy requirements. typical applications include measurement systems, semiconductor technology, optics, medical devices, and automation.

name: Telescopic rail guide
definition: telescopic rail guide systems are linear systems made up of multiple nested rails, allowing long travel distances within a compact installation length. they typically consist of two to three stages and enable partial, full, or over-extension movement. with integrated ball cages or roller guides, they provide stable and smooth motion even under load. telescopic rails are commonly used in drawers, enclosures, machine covers, and maintenance access systems.

name: Trapezoidal screw drive
definition: trapezoidal screw drives are mechanical drive systems that convert rotary motion into linear motion using a spindle with a trapezoidal thread profile and a matching nut. they are known for their high self-locking capability, robust design, and suitability for low to medium-speed positioning tasks. the trapezoidal thread form provides a large contact surface, enabling efficient force transmission and long service life. typical applications include adjustment mechanisms, lifting systems, clamping devices, and linear actuators.

name: Ball screw drive
definition: ball screw drives are high-precision screw drives that convert rotary motion into linear motion using a threaded spindle and a nut with circulating ball bearings. the rolling elements drastically reduce friction, resulting in high efficiency, low wear, and very accurate positioning. ball screws can achieve high feed speeds and support significant loads. they are commonly used in machine tools, automation systems, medical devices, and precision drives.

name: Roller screw drive
definition: roller screw drives are high-precision screw drives in which cylindrical rollers act as rolling elements between the spindle and nut instead of balls. due to the larger contact surface, they provide very high load capacity, rigidity, and positioning accuracy. they are ideal for high-force, continuous-duty, and precision-controlled applications. typical uses include injection molding machines, presses, machine tools, and heavy-duty linear axes.

name: Gear rack drive
definition: rack and pinion drives are mechanical systems that convert rotary motion into linear motion, consisting of a gear (pinion) and a toothed rail (rack). when the pinion rotates, the rack moves linearly through meshing teeth that transfer the force. rack and pinion systems allow for unlimited travel distances, high feed forces, and precise positioning – especially over long axes. typical applications include machine tools, gantry systems, conveyors, and automation equipment.

name: Toothed belt drive
definition: toothed belt drives are positive-fit transmission systems consisting of an endless toothed belt and at least two pulleys with matching teeth. the belt meshes precisely with the pulleys, ensuring slip-free power transmission. toothed belt drives are ideal for precise linear motion at high speeds and enable dynamic positioning with low maintenance. they are commonly used in handling axes, 3d printers, packaging machines, and automation systems.

name: Chain drive (Linear motion technology)
definition: chain drives in linear motion systems use a roller chain guided over sprockets to produce a controlled linear movement. the chain is connected to a carriage or pusher that moves linearly as the chain circulates. chain drives are highly robust, suitable for long travel distances, and capable of transmitting high tensile forces. typical applications include conveyor systems, adjustable axes, heavy-duty motion, and outdoor environments with heavy contamination.

name: Linear motion table
definition: a linear table is a pre-assembled, compact unit designed for precise linear motion, consisting of a guide and a movable carriage or table. depending on the guiding technology used (e.g., plain, ball, or roller guides), linear tables differ in load capacity, precision, and dynamic performance. they are used in mechanical engineering, lab automation, medical devices, and handling systems. various sizes, materials, and configurations are available.

name: Linear motion slide
definition: a linear slide is a movable guiding component that performs linear motion along a fixed guide unit. it is responsible for carrying loads and enabling precise, low-backlash movement. depending on the guiding technology used, linear slides vary in load capacity, friction, dynamics, and precision. they are essential components in mechanical engineering, automation, medical technology, and robotics.

name: Linear motion module, Linear motion axis
definition: a linear module is a rodless actuator that performs a linear movement using an attached or (partially) integrated motor (optionally with a drive controller). the linear motion is generated by an integrated screw or belt drive together with a connected carriage or table part.

name: Electromechanical cylinder
definition: An electromechanical cylinder is an actuator that performs a linear movement using an attached or (partially) integrated motor (optionally with a drive controller). The linear motion is generated by a screw or belt drive together with a connected piston rod.

name: Electromechanical lifting column
definition: An electromechanical lifting column is a linear actuator with integrated guidance and lifting mechanism, enabling vertical movement via an electric motor. It typically consists of a telescopic housing with an internal spindle or rack-and-pinion drive. The column combines guiding and driving functions and is widely used in height-adjustable systems such as workstations, medical equipment, or industrial applications.

name: Electromechanical lifting element
definition: An electromechanical lifting element is an actuator that generates linear lifting motion using an electric motor. The motion is typically transmitted via a spindle, belt, or chain mechanism. Such lifting units are mainly used for basic lifting or adjustment tasks with moderate force and accuracy. They are found in automation, assembly systems, or ergonomic applications.

name: Electromechanical chain guide
definition: An electromechanical chain drive is a linear actuator that uses a motor-driven chain link system to generate linear motion. The chain is wound or unwound to transmit motion to a pusher or guide element. These drives are ideal for compact installations or applications with long strokes. Typical uses include window openers, cover drives, and automation systems.

name: Linear lifting magnet
definition: A linear lifting magnet is an electromechanical device that produces short linear motion when voltage is applied. It consists of a coil and a movable plunger that is displaced linearly by the magnetic field. Linear solenoids are typically used for fast switching operations or actuation tasks with short strokes. Common applications include locking mechanisms, sorting systems, and mechanical interlocks.

name: Linear interlocking magnet
definition: A linear locking magnet is an electromagnetic actuator that extends or retracts a mechanical lock in a linear direction. It is mainly used for safety or holding functions where a specific position must be maintained or released. Depending on the design, return movement is achieved via spring force or reverse polarity. Typical applications include machine covers, safety doors, and industrial locking systems.

name: Electromechanical rotary actuator
definition: An electromechanical rotary actuator is an actuator that generates a rotary motion by means of a mounted or (partially) integrated motor, optionally including a drive controller.

name: Function-oriented drive (electric)
definition: function-oriented drive is an electrically powered drive unit specifically designed to perform a defined function within a technical system – such as lifting, swiveling, stopping, or positioning. Unlike standardized individual components, this drive is tailored to its intended application and is often modular in design. It may include linear actuators, rotary actuators, or specialized drives with integrated electronics. The focus is on providing a clearly defined motion or force transmission as part of a larger functional module or system.

name: Linear rod
definition: a linear rod is a rod-shaped linkage used to transmit linear motion. it transfers force between moving components, such as between an actuator and a load.

definition: this classification encompasses electric motors designed to operate with low voltage in a three-phase alternating current environment, specifically utilizing asynchronous technology. These motors are characterized by their ability to maintain a constant speed under varying load conditions, making them suitable for a range of industrial and commercial applications. The design may include different rotor types, such as squirrel-cage or slip-ring configurations, which influence performance and operational efficiency. Additionally, the classification includes variants that allow for pole-switching functionality, enhancing versatility in applications where speed adjustment is necessary. This category distinguishes itself from other types of motors based on voltage, phase, and operational principles, ensuring clarity in selection and application for users.

name: High voltage three-phase current asynchronous motor
definition: this category encompasses electromechanical devices designed to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy, specifically operating on high voltage three-phase alternating current. These machines are characterized by their asynchronous operation, which allows them to run at a speed that is not synchronized with the frequency of the current supply. The devices within this classification usually feature either squirrel-cage or slip-ring rotors, and they are commonly employed in industrial applications where high power and efficiency are required. The classification distinguishes these motors from various other types of electrical motors based on their voltage ratings, operational principles, and rotor designs, catering to specific performance and application needs in the field of electrical drive technology.

name: Single-phase alternating current motor

These motors are characterized by their ability to operate on a single-phase electrical supply, making them suitable for a variety of applications where three-phase power is not available. The category includes various types of motors that utilize different starting and operational principles, tailored for specific performance requirements. The devices within this classification are commonly used in household appliances, small machine tools, and other applications where moderate power levels are sufficient. Their design may incorporate features that enhance efficiency, facilitate easy installation, and ensure adaptability to various operational conditions.

name: Synchronous motor
definition: a machine designed to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy through the principles of electromagnetism, specifically utilizing synchronous rotation to achieve a constant speed that is synchronized with the frequency of the supply current. This type of motor operates by maintaining a constant speed regardless of load variations, making it suitable for applications requiring precise speed control and efficiency. It can be distinguished from other motor types by its operation principles and construction, which typically includes a rotor and stator designed to create a magnetic field that rotates in unison with the electric current. Variants may include different specifications and configurations to cater to specific industrial or commercial applications.

These engines are designed to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy, providing motion for various applications. They are characterized by their operational efficiency, control capabilities, and adaptability to different driving applications. This category includes engines specifically defined by international standards, as well as those that may have variations or specialized functions. Additionally, it covers advanced motor technologies that utilize ultrasonic principles for movement. This classification serves as a comprehensive reference for identifying and distinguishing various direct current engine technologies and their functionalities in the context of electrical drives.

definition: this category encompasses electromechanical devices designed to provide precise control of angular or linear position, velocity, and acceleration. These devices are characterized by their ability to operate in closed-loop systems, where feedback mechanisms continuously adjust the performance based on desired outcomes. They are utilized in applications requiring accurate motion control, such as robotics, automation, and CNC machinery. The types included within this classification feature various motor technologies that enhance control precision and response times. The offerings in this category emphasize high performance and reliability, catering to industries that demand sophisticated motion solutions.

The focus is on technologies that convert electrical energy into linear displacement, allowing for precise control in applications requiring straight-line motion. The category includes various types of linear motors, each with unique operational characteristics and applications, such as those utilizing direct current, stepping mechanisms, servo control, synchronous operation, or ultrasonic principles. These devices are essential in automation, robotics, and other fields where linear movement is crucial.

This type of machinery typically incorporates multiple windings and a rotor system that facilitates efficient power transmission and conversion, allowing for enhanced performance in various applications. It is characterized by its ability to operate at different load conditions while maintaining optimal efficiency and torque output. This category encompasses a range of machines that are primarily utilized in industrial settings and advanced automation systems, providing reliable and precise control in mechanical operations.

The classification includes variants that feature electronic adjustments, mechanical adjustments, and specific configurations tailored for distinct operational requirements. It serves as a comprehensive reference for identifying and categorizing gear motors that are used in a range of industrial and commercial applications, emphasizing their role in facilitating precise motion control and power transmission.

definition: a device designed to convert electrical frequency and control the operation of electrical motors, optimizing their performance across various applications. This technology allows for the adjustment of motor speed and torque by altering the frequency and voltage supplied to the motor. It serves a critical role in enhancing energy efficiency and improving system responsiveness in industrial and commercial settings. The offerings in this classification include various components that support the functioning and integration of frequency conversion systems, such as modules for control, communication, and braking, as well as capacitors and supply units specifically designed for frequency converters.

name: Paramagnetism, O2 measuring (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed for the measurement and analysis of paramagnetic properties, particularly in the context of gas concentration and composition. These instruments utilize principles of magnetism to detect and quantify the presence of specific gases, providing critical data for various industrial, environmental, and research applications. The focus is on technologies that are specifically tailored to analyze paramagnetic substances, differentiating them from other analytical devices that may operate on different physical principles or target distinct properties. The category supports a diverse range of applications, ensuring accurate and reliable measurements in complex environments where paramagnetic analysis is essential.

name: Fluid analysis appliance
definition: a collection of devices designed to analyze the properties and characteristics of fluids through various measurement techniques. These instruments are utilized to determine composition, concentration, and other relevant parameters of liquid or gas samples. They employ methods that may include spectroscopic, chromatographic, or electrochemical approaches to provide precise data for scientific, industrial, or environmental applications. The appliances in this category are distinguished by their specialized functionalities, enabling users to conduct in-depth evaluations and ensure compliance with quality standards in diverse fields such as chemistry, biology, and engineering. These devices facilitate critical decision-making processes by delivering accurate and reliable analytical results.

name: Photometer, dispersion photometer, diffraction (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices used for measuring light dispersion properties and diffraction patterns within various materials. Such instruments are designed to analyze the behavior of light as it interacts with particles, enabling the assessment of size distributions and concentration levels. The technology applied can vary, utilizing different methodologies to achieve accurate and reliable results. These devices serve critical functions in research and quality control across multiple industries, providing essential data for material characterization and evaluation. The precision and versatility of these measuring instruments make them indispensable in applications requiring detailed analysis of particulate matter and light interaction phenomena.

name: Refractometer, polarimeter (PAT)
definition: this category encompasses analytical instruments specifically designed for measuring the refractive index and optical rotation of substances. These devices are essential in various scientific and industrial applications, providing crucial data for quality control, material characterization, and research purposes. Instruments in this classification are characterized by their ability to analyze the properties of liquids and solids through the interaction of light with matter, allowing for precise determinations that aid in the formulation and assessment of materials. The tools included are vital for industries such as pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, and petrochemicals, where understanding the optical characteristics of substances is paramount.

name: Mass spectrometer (MS, PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed for the analysis and measurement of mass and composition of substances through the application of mass spectrometry techniques. These instruments operate by ionizing chemical species and sorting the ions based on their mass-to-charge ratios. They are pivotal in various scientific fields, providing insights into molecular structures, chemical compositions, and isotopic ratios. The devices within this classification are distinguished by their specific methodologies and operational principles, allowing for precise quantitative and qualitative analysis of samples. This classification does not include other analytical devices focused on different measurement principles or technologies.

name: Chromatograph, separation technique (GC,LC,PAT)
definition: this category encompasses devices and technologies specifically designed for the separation and analysis of chemical mixtures. These instruments utilize various methodologies to separate components based on their physical or chemical properties, facilitating the qualitative and quantitative analysis of substances. The devices in this classification are essential for applications in laboratories and industrial settings, enabling researchers and professionals to obtain detailed insights into complex samples. The focus is on techniques that enhance the efficiency and accuracy of separation processes, contributing to advancements in fields such as chemistry, pharmaceuticals, and environmental analysis. Each type of instrument within this category operates on distinct principles and is suited for specific analytical tasks, ensuring comprehensive coverage of separation techniques.

name: PH, redox, conductivity (PAT)
definition: this category encompasses various devices and instruments designed for the measurement and analysis of chemical properties related to pH, redox potential, and electrical conductivity. These devices are essential in various scientific, industrial, and environmental applications, providing precise data that informs processes and decision-making. They include specialized sensors and transducers that detect and quantify the concentration of ions in a solution, as well as electrodes that facilitate these measurements. The instruments may vary in technology and design, but they all serve the common purpose of analyzing the chemical behavior of substances in different environments, ensuring accurate monitoring and control in diverse applications.

name: Electrochemical sensor for pH, redox, conductivity (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed specifically for measuring electrochemical properties such as pH, redox potential, and conductivity. These instruments utilize electrochemical principles to provide insights into the chemical composition and behavior of various substances. They are essential tools in analytical chemistry and environmental monitoring, playing a crucial role in applications where precise measurement of ionic concentrations and redox states is necessary. The devices can be employed in diverse fields, including laboratory analysis, industrial processes, and quality control, facilitating the assessment of water quality, chemical reactions, and other critical parameters. Through their specialized functionalities, these instruments contribute significantly to data-driven decision-making in scientific and industrial contexts.

name: Measuring system with material specific auxiliary reaction (PAT)
definition: this category encompasses systems designed for precise measurement and analysis that involve the use of material-specific auxiliary reactions. Such systems are essential in various scientific and industrial applications, where the interaction between the measuring device and the material being analyzed is critical for obtaining accurate results. The focus is on technologies that facilitate the detection, quantification, or characterization of specific properties or components within a sample, utilizing auxiliary reactions tailored to the material's nature. These systems play a vital role in enhancing measurement accuracy and reliability across diverse fields.

name: FID, TOC, TN (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices and technologies utilized for the analysis and measurement of various properties and substances in a range of applications. It includes equipment designed for assessing material characteristics through specific analytical methods, focusing on the detection and quantification of chemical and physical properties. The devices listed under this classification are essential for researchers and professionals who require precise and reliable data for scientific studies, quality control, or environmental monitoring. This category emphasizes methodologies that involve oxidation processes and detection techniques, highlighting the importance of accurate measurement in both laboratory and field settings.

name: Moisture measurement (non-radiometric, PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices and systems designed to measure moisture content using various non-radiometric techniques. These measurement methods are instrumental in providing accurate assessments of moisture levels in different materials and environments without the application of radiometric technology. The focus is on innovative approaches that leverage principles such as capacitance, electrochemistry, optics, and microwave technology to achieve precise moisture determination. The offerings within this classification are essential for applications across industries where moisture measurement is critical for quality control, process optimization, and product performance. Each device is characterized by its unique operational principles and measurement capabilities, ensuring a diverse range of solutions tailored to specific measurement needs.

name: Radiometry (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices and systems designed for the measurement of radiant energy and its properties. These tools are utilized to assess various forms of radiation, including light, infrared, and other electromagnetic waves. They play a critical role in scientific research, industrial applications, and environmental monitoring, providing essential data for analysis and decision-making processes. The instruments included in this category are specifically engineered to detect and quantify radiation emitted from various sources, ensuring accuracy and reliability in measurements. Additionally, it covers supporting components that enhance the functionality and effectiveness of the primary measuring devices, facilitating precise and comprehensive radiometric assessments.

name: Calorimeter, ex-monitoring (PAT)
definition: this category encompasses devices specifically designed to measure the thermal properties of substances, particularly focusing on the calorimetry of various materials. These instruments are utilized to determine heat transfer, energy changes, and thermal characteristics, providing critical data for research, quality control, and process optimization. They may be employed in a range of applications, including but not limited to, industrial processes, environmental monitoring, and scientific research. Instruments in this classification may vary in their operational principles and measurement techniques, often tailored for specific types of materials such as fluids or gases. The devices are essential for understanding energy dynamics in chemical reactions and physical processes, thereby contributing to advancements in technology and science.

name: Viscosimeter (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices specifically designed for measuring the viscosity of fluids, which is a key parameter in characterizing the flow behavior of various substances. Such devices are essential in numerous industries, including pharmaceuticals, food and beverage, and chemical manufacturing, where the viscosity of a product can significantly impact its processing and application. The technology utilized may vary, incorporating different methods such as oscillation, orifice, and surface measurements to obtain accurate viscosity readings. This classification distinguishes these devices from others in the realm of analysis technology by focusing solely on viscosity measurement applications, ensuring that each item within this category is tailored to meet the unique demands of viscosity analysis in diverse material states and conditions.

name: Thermal conductivity (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices and technologies specifically designed for the assessment and quantification of thermal conductivity properties in various materials. It includes instruments that provide accurate measurements of heat transfer capabilities, essential for evaluating material performance in thermal management applications. The focus is on methodologies that allow for the determination of thermal conductivity through different testing techniques, ensuring reliability and precision in results. This category is distinct from other analytical technologies that measure different physical properties or utilize alternative measurement principles, maintaining a clear focus on thermal conductivity analysis and related measurement processes.

name: Sound, ultrasonic level measurement (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices specifically designed for measuring levels using ultrasonic technology. These instruments utilize high-frequency sound waves to determine the distance to a surface or the level of a substance within a container. They are characterized by their non-contact measurement capabilities, making them suitable for a variety of applications in diverse environments. This category includes systems that operate based on the reflection of ultrasonic waves and those that analyze the time it takes for the sound waves to return after bouncing off a target. The accuracy and reliability of these devices make them essential tools in various industries, including manufacturing, environmental monitoring, and process control. The focus is on their ability to provide precise level measurements without the need for direct contact with the material being measured.

name: Tensiometer (PAT)
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed to measure surface tension or interfacial tension within various substances. These instruments operate based on different principles and methodologies to provide accurate readings relevant to specific applications in both research and industrial contexts. definition: this classification encompasses systems and devices specifically designed for the management and automation of motion in various applications. These solutions enable precise control over movement parameters, integrating hardware and software components to facilitate programmable operations. The focus is on technologies that enhance the performance and efficiency of motion control processes, offering versatility for diverse operational requirements. This category includes various methodologies for motion control, such as computer-based, controller-based, and drive-based systems, alongside essential components that support functionality, communication, power supply, and internal connections. It also emphasizes the design and integration aspects necessary for effective project implementation in motion control contexts.

name: NC (numerical control)
definition: this classification encompasses systems and components designed for numerical control applications, which enable the automated control of machinery and processes through programmed instructions. These systems utilize various controllers and peripherals to achieve precise operation, enhancing efficiency and accuracy in industrial settings. The classification includes both PC-based and controller-based solutions, along with essential components such as analog and digital peripherals, communication interfaces, power supplies, and internal connection systems. Each item within this classification serves a critical role in enabling effective numerical control solutions, facilitating integration into broader process control systems while differentiating from other control methodologies.

name: Programmable logic control (SPS)
definition: this classification encompasses programmable logic controllers designed to automate industrial processes through programmable instructions. These devices facilitate the control of machinery and equipment by executing predetermined logic sequences and processes. The focus is on modular components that enhance the functionality and adaptability of the control system, including input/output modules that manage signals from sensors and actuators, communication modules that ensure data exchange between devices, and basic devices that serve as the core of the control system. Additional elements include functional modules that provide specialized capabilities, memory units for data storage, and simulation modules for testing and validation purposes. This classification distinctly separates these devices from other control technologies, emphasizing their programmable nature and versatility in various automation applications.

name: Operate and Observe (HMI)
definition: this classification encompasses devices and systems designed to facilitate the operation and monitoring of processes, focusing on human-machine interaction. It includes various interfaces and appliances that enable users to manage and observe process control systems effectively. The items categorized here support functionalities such as safety interventions, signal transmission, and operational commands, ensuring efficient communication between the user and the process. Additionally, they may feature specialized terminals designed for hazardous environments, providing essential operational capabilities. This classification distinctly separates these items from other control technologies, emphasizing their unique role in enhancing the interaction and oversight of process systems.

name: Control software
definition: this classification encompasses software solutions specifically designed for managing and optimizing control processes within various systems. It includes tools that facilitate the programming, engineering, and visualization of control tasks, as well as application-oriented software that supports specific functionalities related to control systems. Additionally, this category features function modules and libraries that enhance the capabilities of control software, as well as documentation resources that provide essential information for users and developers. The offerings within this classification focus on improving efficiency, usability, and integration in control environments, distinguishing them from other control-related software solutions.

name: Field bus, decentralized peripheral
definition: this classification encompasses devices specifically designed to facilitate communication and control within decentralized automation systems. These devices are integral components that enable the connection and interaction between various field devices and a central control system. They support both analog and digital signal processing and include various modules that serve distinct functions, such as input/output processing, communication, and power management. The offerings in this category are characterized by their ability to operate in a distributed manner, allowing for flexible and scalable automation solutions. Their design is optimized for integration into a wider process control framework, ensuring efficient operation across diverse industrial applications.

name: Control component
definition: this category encompasses devices and systems designed to manage and regulate the operation of various processes and machinery. It includes components that enable the adjustment of performance parameters, enhance efficiency, and ensure system stability. These items facilitate the integration of various control functions within a broader operational framework. The focus is on components that can be tailored or configured to meet specific operational requirements, rather than fixed-function devices or software solutions. This classification highlights the versatility and adaptability of these control elements in diverse applications, emphasizing their role in optimizing and maintaining effective process control systems.

name: Capacitor
definition: a passive electronic component characterized by its ability to store and release electrical energy. This component typically consists of two conductive plates separated by an insulating material (dielectric). It is utilized in various applications to manage voltage fluctuations, filter signals, and smooth out power supplies. The classification within this category includes various types based on construction materials and functionality, such as those made from ceramics, films, electrolytic substances, and mica. Additionally, there are types that allow for variable capacitance adjustments, catering to specific tuning and preset applications. This classification encompasses components essential for circuit design and performance optimization in electronic devices.

name: Inductor (electronics)
definition: in general, a component having self inductance that is manufactured by winding a conductor on the surface of an insulation

name: Refrigeration equipment (electronic component)
definition: this classification encompasses equipment designed for refrigeration purposes that incorporates electronic components. These items are utilized in various cooling and temperature control applications. The classification focuses on devices that actively manage thermal conditions, ensuring efficient heat exchange and temperature maintenance. It distinguishes itself from other electronic components through its specific function related to refrigeration technology. This category may include various electronic assemblies and systems that contribute to the operation and efficiency of refrigeration devices, highlighting their role in temperature regulation and energy management. An example of an item included in this classification is a heat sink, which plays a crucial role in dissipating heat generated by electronic components in refrigeration systems.

name: Conductor board (unpopulated)
definition: a platform designed to support electronic components, featuring designated areas for the placement of various parts without any pre-installed elements. This structure is primarily utilized in the assembly of electronic devices, allowing for the connection and integration of diverse electronic parts. It serves as a foundational layer where additional components can be mounted, providing the necessary electrical connections and mechanical stability. This category distinguishes itself from other electronic components by focusing on the foundational aspect rather than the functionality of specific active or passive elements. Variants within this category accommodate different levels of flexibility and configuration, enabling tailored solutions for various electronic applications.

name: Memory Chip
definition: integrated circuit consisting of memory cells for storing and retrieving data and usually including associated circuits such as those for address selection, amplifiers, etc

name: Discrete component
definition: this classification encompasses electronic components that are distinct, individual units designed for specific electronic functions. These components are typically characterized by their ability to control and manipulate electrical signals. They play critical roles in a wide range of applications, including signal processing, power management, and signal modulation. The items classified within this category include specific types of semiconductor devices that are integral to electronic circuits, enabling functions such as rectification, amplification, and switching. Each component is engineered to perform distinct electrical tasks independently, contributing to the overall functionality and efficiency of electronic systems.

name: Logic-component
definition: a collection of electronic components specifically designed to perform logical operations, manipulate information, or facilitate decision-making processes within electronic systems. These components are essential in the construction of circuits that handle digital signals and data processing tasks. They may include various types of integrated circuits, such as those designed for arithmetic operations, comparison functions, and data storage. This category encompasses devices that operate on binary values, enabling complex functionality in computing and control applications. The classification includes products that contribute to the overall efficiency and capability of electronic devices in various technological environments.

name: Opto-component
definition: this classification encompasses devices that utilize optical principles and are essential in various electronic applications. These components are characterized by their ability to emit, detect, or manipulate light and electromagnetic radiation across different wavelengths. They play a crucial role in enhancing the functionality of electronic systems by facilitating communication, sensing, and energy conversion. The items classified here include those that operate in the visible spectrum, as well as in the infrared and ultraviolet ranges. Their applications span diverse fields such as telecommunications, consumer electronics, automotive systems, and industrial automation, making them vital for modern technological advancements.

name: Analogue component
definition: this classification encompasses various electronic components that operate using analogue principles. These components are essential for processing continuous signals and are integral to a wide range of electronic circuits. They are characterized by their ability to handle varying signal amplitudes, providing crucial functionality in communication, signal conditioning, and control systems. The items classified within this category include specialized devices designed for specific applications, enhancing the performance and efficiency of electronic systems. Their roles often involve amplification, signal filtering, tuning, voltage regulation, and other functions that facilitate the manipulation of analogue signals in electronic designs. These components are vital for ensuring optimal operation in both consumer and industrial electronics.

name: Application specific semiconductor
definition: this category encompasses specialized electronic components that are designed and optimized for specific applications. These components are integral to various electronic systems, providing tailored functionality that meets the unique requirements of particular tasks or processes. This classification highlights devices that often integrate multiple functions or features within a single unit, resulting in enhanced performance and efficiency in their designated applications. Examples include processing units that handle complex calculations, integrated circuits that execute specific tasks, and sensors that monitor and respond to environmental conditions. The focus is on components that enable advanced capabilities in electronic designs, supporting innovation across diverse fields.

name: Display (liquid crystal)
definition: this classification encompasses devices that utilize liquid crystal technology to display visual information. These items are characterized by their ability to modulate light through the alignment of liquid crystals, offering high-resolution imagery and energy efficiency. Applications typically include various types of screens and monitors found in consumer electronics, industrial equipment, and other visual display systems. The classification distinguishes these devices from other electronic components that serve different functions, such as those related to energy storage, signal processing, or power management. Included within this classification are both active and passive types of liquid crystal displays, each with distinct operational capabilities and applications.

name: Tube connector (component)
definition: this category encompasses connectors designed specifically for tubes, serving as critical components within electronic systems. These connectors facilitate the secure and efficient joining of various electronic parts, ensuring reliable signal transmission and power distribution. They are integral to the assembly and functionality of electronic devices, enabling seamless integration between different elements. The focus is on components that connect tubular structures, distinguishing them from other electronic components such as resistors, capacitors, and inductors. This classification includes items like sockets tailored for different display technologies, highlighting the versatility and application of tube connectors in various electronic setups.

name: Resonator
definition: a resonator is a device that exhibits resonant behavior, typically used to control the frequency of electronic circuits. It operates by oscillating at a specific frequency, allowing for the filtering and stabilization of signals in various applications. This component is essential in communications, timing applications, and signal processing, where precise frequency control is paramount. Unlike passive components that simply resist, store, or conduct electrical energy, the resonator actively participates in the generation and regulation of frequencies. It can be utilized in a variety of electronic systems, from simple oscillators to complex communication devices, enhancing performance and reliability by ensuring signal integrity and stability. The resonator's role is critical in applications requiring accurate timing and frequency reference.

name: Radio wave absorber
definition: this classification encompasses materials specifically designed to absorb radio waves, effectively reducing electromagnetic interference in electronic devices. These absorbers are utilized in various applications, such as telecommunications, aerospace, and consumer electronics, to enhance signal quality and performance. The types of absorbers covered include those made from specialized ferrite materials, composite carbon structures, magnetic composites, and conductive substances. This category distinguishes itself from other electronic components by its primary function of wave absorption rather than energy storage or signal modulation, highlighting its role in improving the efficiency and reliability of electronic systems through effective electromagnetic management.

A singleturn version measures the absolute position within a revolution. A multiturn version measures the absolute position over several revolutions. Intended for use in safety applications

These devices operate by emitting ultrasonic waves and interpreting the reflected signals to ascertain the presence or distance of nearby objects. The emphasis is on features that enhance safety, making them suitable for use in critical systems where reliable detection is paramount. Unlike other sensing technologies, this classification is distinguished by its unique operating principles and safety enhancements, ensuring compliance with safety standards while providing precise measurement and detection capabilities in diverse operational contexts.

The offerings in this category include various types of sensors that may operate through different principles, such as contact or non-contact methods, and are integral to automation and process optimization. The devices are characterized by their application in environments where precision and reliability are paramount, often interfacing with control systems for real-time data acquisition and feedback.

name: Flow sensor
definition: Flow sensors (also flowmeters) sense the physical quantity of flow of a gas or liquid through a pipe and convert this into an electrical output value as a measure of the flow or directly indicate it with a display. The measured value is given as volume flow, which indicates how much volume of a medium is transported through a specified cross-section per period of time, or as mass flow, which indicates the mass of a medium moving through a cross-section per period of time

name: Pressure sensor
definition: Pressure sensors sense the physical quantity of pressure (= force per area) and convert this into an electrical output value as a measure of the pressure. Depending on the measuring method, a distinction is made between absolute pressure sensors, relative pressure sensors and differential pressure sensors

name: Pneumatic sensor
definition: Pneumatic sensors are dynamic pressure-dependent, technical constructions which can detect a measuring object without contact by changes in air jet pressure. 3 pneumatic sensor types can be distinguished 1) pneumatic dynamic pressure sensors ( dynamic nozzles) - 2) pneumatic ring jet sensors (ring jet nozzles) - 3) pneumatic air barrier sensors (air barriers). A pneumatic sensor usually consists of : a pneumatic transmitter nozzle / a pneumatic receiver nozzle / a pneumatic path (air gap) / a pneumatic pressure amplifier (only if necessary) and an electro-pneumatic converter Advantages of pneumatic sensor principles compared to other sensor principles are : Functional reliability in case of dirt accumulation / high ambient temperatures / electromagnetic susceptibility / working in complete darkness / scanning of translucent measuring objects / working in explosion-proof rooms is possible

name: Temperature sensor

This category includes various devices and systems designed to read or write information magnetically, ensuring accurate and reliable identification. The focus is on the mechanisms and applications that leverage magnetic properties, distinguishing them from other identification methods that utilize optical, biometric, inductive, acoustic, electromechanical, microwave, radar, ultrasound, or alternative principles. This classification is essential for industries where magnetic identification plays a crucial role in tracking, access control, and inventory management.

name: Inductive identification
definition: this category encompasses systems and technologies that utilize inductive principles for the purpose of identification. It involves the interaction between electromagnetic fields and conductive materials to facilitate the recognition and tracking of items or entities. These systems are characterized by their ability to operate without direct line-of-sight requirements, enabling seamless identification processes. This classification specifically includes devices that utilize radio frequency identification (RFID) technology, such as readers and transponders, which are designed to capture and transmit unique identifiers associated with tagged objects. The emphasis is on the inductive method of operation, distinguishing it from other identification technologies based on different physical principles.

name: Acoustic identification
definition: this classification encompasses methods and technologies that utilize sound waves for the purpose of recognizing or verifying identities. It includes processes that rely on acoustic signals to capture and analyze unique auditory characteristics or patterns. The focus is on distinguishing entities based on sound-based interactions, which can involve direct acoustic measurements, signal processing techniques, or the interpretation of auditory data. This category excludes other identification methods that rely on visual cues, biometric traits, magnetic properties, inductive mechanisms, electromechanical systems, or non-acoustic technologies. Products and services within this classification are specifically tailored to facilitate or enhance identification processes through acoustic means.

name: Electromechanical identification
definition: this category encompasses devices and systems that utilize electromechanical processes for the purpose of identifying, tracking, or managing assets and individuals. These solutions typically combine electronic and mechanical components to deliver unique identification capabilities. Products within this classification may involve the use of chip cards, which store data electronically and can be used for a variety of applications, including secure access and transaction processing. Additionally, hybrid systems that integrate both chip card technology and magnetic elements are included, offering versatility in identification methods. Cleaning cards designed for maintaining the functionality of identification devices are also part of this category. The focus is on electromechanical approaches, distinguishing them from other identification methods that rely on optical, biometric, magnetic, inductive, acoustic, microwave, radar, ultrasound, or other principles.

name: Identification using microwave
definition: this classification encompasses systems and technologies that utilize microwave signals for the purpose of identifying objects, individuals, or data. It includes methods that rely on the unique interactions between microwaves and the target, enabling accurate detection and recognition. The focus is on non-invasive identification techniques that leverage the properties of microwave radiation, distinguishing them from other identification methodologies such as visual, biometric, magnetic, inductive, acoustic, electromechanical, radar-based, or ultrasound approaches. This category serves various applications across industries, facilitating efficient and reliable identification processes through microwave technology.

name: Identification using radar
definition: this category encompasses methods and technologies that utilize radar systems for the identification of objects, individuals, or phenomena. It includes various applications where radar waves are emitted, reflected, and analyzed to ascertain characteristics or determine the presence of targets. The focus is on non-intrusive techniques that leverage the unique properties of radar signals, distinguishing them from other identification methods such as optical, biometric, or magnetic techniques. This classification is relevant in diverse fields, including security, transportation, and environmental monitoring, where radar technology provides reliable and efficient identification capabilities.

name: Identification using ultrasound

It includes various applications where ultrasound waves are employed to capture, analyze, and interpret data for recognizing or verifying objects, individuals, or conditions. This classification is distinct from other identification methods that rely on different physical principles or technologies, such as optical, biometric, magnetic, inductive, acoustic, electromechanical, microwave, and radar techniques. The focus here is on ultrasound's unique capabilities, which may involve measuring sound wave reflection, transmission, or absorption characteristics to achieve accurate identification results.

name: Identification, other principles

These methods may involve unique algorithms, systems, or technologies that differentiate them from standard identification methods. The focus is on technologies that support operational efficiency, accuracy, and compliance with industry standards while addressing the unique demands of various industrial processes.

name: Industrial weighing technology, continuous

name: Gate valve
definition: a type of valve designed to control the flow of fluids through a piping system by lifting or lowering a gate, which is a barrier that either allows or restricts the passage of fluid. This mechanism enables a full flow when open and creates a tight seal when closed, making it suitable for applications requiring minimal flow resistance. Typically constructed from various materials, including metals and plastics, the design prioritizes durability and efficiency in managing fluid dynamics. This classification focuses specifically on variants that do not feature an actuator and includes specific applications like waste management systems.

name: Globe valve
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed to regulate or control the flow of liquids or gases within a piping system. Characterized by their spherical shape and internal mechanism, these fittings provide the functionality of both shutting off and modulating flow. Generally constructed from durable materials, they are engineered to withstand high pressures and temperatures, ensuring reliable operation in various applications. The offerings within this category include variants that cater to specific operational needs, such as those designed for shut-off purposes, flow control, or integration into more complex systems. Their design facilitates easy installation and maintenance, making them essential components in industrial, commercial, and residential settings where precise flow management is crucial.

name: Butterfly valve
definition: a type of valve characterized by a disc that pivots around a central point to regulate fluid flow within a piping system. This device is commonly utilized in various applications due to its ability to provide quick shut-off and precise control. Typically constructed from materials such as metal or plastic, this fitting is designed for durability and efficiency in fluid management. Its operational mechanism allows for minimal pressure drop and a streamlined flow path, making it suitable for both on-off and throttling service. This category includes variations specifically designed for hydraulic systems, highlighting its versatility in industrial and commercial settings.

name: Ball valve
definition: a device designed to control the flow of fluids, characterized by a spherical closure element that rotates to open or close the passage. This mechanism allows for quick and efficient regulation, providing a reliable sealing capability when fully closed. Typically constructed from durable materials, such as metals or plastics, these devices are used in various applications across industries. Their design facilitates minimal resistance to flow, ensuring optimal performance in systems requiring precise flow management. This classification encompasses various configurations and sizes, catering to diverse operational needs, while distinguishing itself from other valve types based on functionality and structural design.

name: Condensate draining fitting
definition: this classification encompasses devices specifically designed to facilitate the efficient removal of condensate from various systems. These fittings are engineered to manage the flow of liquid, ensuring that condensate is appropriately directed or disposed of to prevent system inefficiencies or damage. The category includes various types of traps that employ different mechanisms to capture and discharge condensate, thereby optimizing performance and maintaining operational integrity. The focus is on fittings that contribute to the effective management of condensate within piping systems, distinguished by their unique operational characteristics and applications.

name: Reflux fitting
definition: a type of device designed to manage the flow of fluids in a piping system, ensuring that the fluid moves in a single direction while preventing backflow. This component is essential in various applications where contamination or reverse flow could cause system inefficiencies or failures. Typically constructed from either metal or plastic, it serves to maintain system integrity and protect downstream components. The design may vary to accommodate different operational requirements, including the use of gravity or mechanical mechanisms for functionality. This category encompasses specific variants that include features aimed at optimizing performance in fluid transport systems.

name: Safety fitting
definition: this category encompasses devices designed to ensure the safe operation of systems by preventing overpressure, controlling flow, and managing potential hazards. These fittings are crucial in safeguarding equipment and personnel from risks associated with pressure variations, explosive conditions, or uncontrolled fluid release. The devices included in this classification serve specific functions to maintain safety standards in various applications, providing mechanisms to relieve excess pressure, contain potential hazards, and ensure reliable shutdown procedures. They represent essential components in systems where safety is paramount, contributing to the overall integrity and reliability of operational processes.

name: Valve (with actuator)
definition: this category encompasses various types of valves equipped with actuators, designed for controlling the flow of fluids in different applications. These devices are essential components in systems requiring precise regulation and automation of fluid movement. The inclusion of actuators allows for remote operation and enhanced efficiency in managing flow, pressure, and direction. This classification distinguishes itself from other valve types that do not include an actuator or serve different functional purposes. The items within this classification are tailored for diverse industrial, commercial, and residential applications, ensuring reliable performance and compliance with operational standards.

name: Pressure control fitting
definition: a category designated for components designed to manage and regulate pressure within various systems, ensuring optimal performance and safety. These components are essential in controlling the flow and pressure of fluids or gases, often employed in industrial, commercial, or residential settings. They encompass devices that automatically adjust pressure levels, safeguarding equipment and processes from pressure fluctuations. This classification includes instruments specifically engineered for reducing excess pressure, maintaining desired pressure levels, and facilitating precise control of pressure variables. These fittings are critical in applications where pressure stability is paramount, contributing to the efficiency and reliability of fluid transport and handling systems.

name: Pigging system
definition: Component for regulating the flow in pipelines, which can vary the volume inside by introducing quantities of material.

name: Control fitting
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed to regulate, direct, or control the flow of fluids within a system. These components are typically installed within piping or ducting systems and are essential for ensuring efficient operation and safety. They may include mechanisms that allow for the adjustment of flow rates, pressure management, and fluid monitoring. The devices classified here may also involve indicators or gauges that provide visual feedback regarding fluid levels or flow conditions, facilitating operational oversight. The components in this classification are utilized across various applications, contributing to the functionality and reliability of fluid transport systems.

name: Filter, Strainer (fitting)
definition: this classification encompasses devices designed to separate solids from liquids or gases, thereby ensuring the purity and efficiency of fluid systems. These components are typically integrated into piping or ducting systems and are vital for preventing contaminants from entering machinery, pipelines, or other processing equipment. They are distinguished by their filtering capabilities, which can include various filtration methods and materials. The classification specifically excludes other types of flow control devices, emphasizing the unique function of filtration. Examples of specific types within this classification include protective strainers and cartridge filters, which serve to enhance operational reliability and reduce maintenance needs in various applications.

name: Sampling fitting
definition: this classification encompasses fittings specifically designed for sampling purposes within fluid systems. These fittings are integral components that allow for the extraction of small quantities of fluid for analysis or testing, ensuring that the integrity of the system is maintained during the sampling process. The fittings in this category are engineered to facilitate various sampling methods, providing reliable functionality in a range of applications. They are distinct from other types of fittings typically used for controlling flow or pressure, ensuring specialized performance for sampling tasks. Examples of items in this classification include valves and cocks tailored for sampling operations, emphasizing their role in obtaining representative fluid samples without significant disruption to the system.

name: Diaphragm fitting
definition: EN 736-1: valve in which the fluid flow passage through the valve is changed by deformation of a flexible obturator.

name: Valve for suction system
definition: a device designed to regulate the flow of fluids within a suction system, characterized by its ability to direct or control the movement of gases or liquids through pipes or ducts. This category encompasses various types of fittings specifically engineered for suction applications, ensuring optimal performance and efficiency. The classification includes items that serve distinct functions in managing fluid dynamics, thereby enhancing the operational effectiveness of suction systems. Each fitting is tailored to address specific requirements within the suction process, providing solutions for diverse industrial and commercial needs.

name: Tapping fitting
definition: a category encompassing various types of fittings designed specifically for tapping into pipelines or systems, allowing for the extraction or introduction of fluids. These fittings facilitate connections within a piping system and support various operational functionalities, such as controlling flow or enabling maintenance activities. This classification includes a range of designs and materials to suit different applications and environments, ensuring compatibility with existing infrastructure and operational requirements. The focus is on fittings that provide efficient access and management of fluid dynamics, enhancing the overall functionality and reliability of the connected systems.

name: Thermostat fitting
definition: a fitting designed specifically for use with thermostatic control systems, enabling the regulation of temperature within a designated area. This type of fitting typically integrates with heating or cooling systems to maintain desired temperature levels efficiently. It allows for precise control of fluid flow based on temperature variations, contributing to improved energy efficiency and system performance. The construction may involve materials such as metal or plastic, ensuring durability and suitability for various environmental conditions. This classification encompasses specific devices that are tailored for temperature management applications, distinguishing them from other types of fittings that serve different functional purposes in fluid regulation and control.

name: Flange (steel)
definition: this classification encompasses a variety of circular components designed to connect, secure, or seal sections of piping systems made from steel. These items are characterized by their flat surfaces and typically feature holes for bolting to other flanges or equipment, ensuring a tight and leak-proof connection. The range includes various designs and functionalities to accommodate different requirements in industrial applications. Each item in this classification is specifically engineered to withstand pressure and facilitate the flow of fluids or gases within a piping system, offering versatility and reliability in construction and assembly processes.

name: Pipe and threaded tube (steel)
definition: a collection of cylindrical or tubular products made primarily from steel, designed for the transport of fluids or gases. These items feature either threaded ends or are intended for seamless connections, ensuring a secure and reliable flow through various systems. This category encompasses items that may vary in dimensions, wall thickness, and method of manufacture, allowing for versatile applications in construction, industrial processes, and infrastructure. Key characteristics include durability, resistance to corrosion, and the ability to withstand high pressures, making them suitable for a range of environments. The classification excludes related products such as joint connectors and specialized fittings.

name: Fitting (steel)
definition: this category encompasses various components designed to connect or modify the flow within a piping system made of steel materials. These components are essential in facilitating changes in direction, branching, and the overall management of fluid movement within the system.
